RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r7.claim: Human development from a drop is especially clear evidence for a freely choosing, wise Creator because complex human arrangements emerge from simple matter.
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r7.anchor: أن التركيبات العجيبة في بدن الإنسان أكثر ، فيكون تولده عن المادة البسيطة أدل على القادر المختار

RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r8.claim: The sign is especially compelling because people know their own condition better than that of other things.
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r8.anchor: أن اطلاع الإنسان على أحوال نفسه أكثر من اطلاعه على أحوال غيره

RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r9.claim: People continually witness this process in their children and other animals, strengthening the inference to the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r9.anchor: أن مشاهدة الإنسان لهذه الأحوال في أولاده وأولاد سائر الحيوانات دائمة

RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r10.claim: The same proof establishes resurrection: the Creator gathered dispersed matter from the parents and world to form a person, so He can reassemble the dead after their parts disperse.
RAZI-FULL:v31p118/r10.anchor: حدوث الإنسان إنما كان بسبب اجتماع أجزاء كانت متفرقة في بدن الوالدين

STUDYQURAN:86:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r1.claim: Those who deny resurrection should reflect on how God created them.
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r1.anchor: Let those who deny the Resurrection reflect upon the manner in which God created them

STUDYQURAN:86:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r2.claim: The verse can also call people to recognize their purpose in creation, as in the call to worship at 51:56.
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r2.anchor: This verse can also be understood as a call to recognize that for which the human being was created

STUDYQURAN:86:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r3.speaker: Maybudī
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r3.claim: Maybudī describes humans as created for prostration, heed, service, knowledge, and love, with tongues adorned by testimony, hearts by knowledge and joy, and bodies by worship.
STUDYQURAN:86:5/r3.anchor: God created a face fit for prostration, eyes fit for taking heed, a body fit for service, a heart fit for knowledge

TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.claim: He challenges resurrection deniers to inspect their creation from emitted, poured fluid; two unnamed poetic lines use tarāʾib with gold, saffron, neck, and chest imagery as linguistic evidence.
TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.anchor: وقال آخر: [البحر الكامل] والزعفران على ترائبها … شرقا به اللبات والنحر

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.claim: The Angel of Death takes people at death, and God takes souls at death and sleep; angelic preservation can also mean preserving souls through writing their deeds.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.anchor: ولا ينافي هذا الوجه ظاهر آية الانفطار السابقة من أن حفظ الملائكة هو الكتابة

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.claim: An objection says absolute power cannot prove resurrection because recreating the very same human is impossible: a second body would be merely like, not identical to, the first.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.anchor: ومحصله أن إطلاق القدرة إنما ينفع فيما كان ممكنا لكن إعادة الإنسان بعينه محال فإن الإنسان المخلوق ثانيا مثل الانسان الدنيوي

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.claim: The answer is that personal identity resides in the preserved soul, not the body; when that soul joins a recreated body, it is the same person despite bodily similarity.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.anchor: وجه الاندفاع أن شخصية الشخص من الإنسان بنفسه لا ببدنه والنفس محفوظة فإذا خلق البدن وتعلقت به النفس كان هو الإنسان الدنيوي بشخصه

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r4.claim: Since each soul and its deeds are preserved, the human should accept return and recompense, and reflect on his origin in gushing water to see that his creator can resurrect him.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r4.anchor: ومحصل المعنى وإذ كانت كل نفس محفوظة بذاتها وعملها من غير أن تفنى أو ينسى عملها فليذعن الإنسان أن سيرجع إلى ربه

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r5.claim: The passive construction omits God as agent because His role is self-evident; the same implication appears in the next verse's passive construction.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r5.anchor: وترك ذكر الفاعل وهو الله سبحانه إيماء إلى ظهور أمره

TABRISI:86:2-9/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r8.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:86:2-9/r8.claim: The address targets one who denies resurrection: reflect on the source and manner of human creation to recognize that the One who began it from a drop can restore it.

THALABI:v10p179/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p179/r1.claim: The verse asks a person to consider what his Lord created him from.
THALABI:v10p179/r1.anchor: فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق أي من أي شيء خلقه ربه، ثم بين جل ثناؤه فقال سبحانه وتعالى

BURSEVI:v10p309/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r2.claim: The human, compounded of ignorance and forgetfulness and denying resurrection, gathering, and judgment, is urged to consider his origin.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r2.anchor: فلينظر الإنسان} ليتفكر الإنسان المركب من الجهل والنسيان المنكر للنشور والحشر والميزان

BURSEVI:v10p309/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r3.claim: “From what?” is the question; its fuller form is مما, with alif omitted for ease, as in the earlier discussion of 78:1.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r3.anchor: مم} أي من أي شيء فأصله مما حذفت الألف تخفيفا كما مر في عم

BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.claim: Creation from matter untouched by life proves the Creator can restore the dead, indeed more readily by rational analogy, so people should prepare for recompense.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.anchor: من قدر على إنشائه من مواد لم تشم رائحة الحياة قط فهو قادر على إعادته بل أقدر على قياس العقل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r1.claim: Muqātil takes the person being addressed as the one who denies resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني: (الذي يكون منه) (¬2) المكذب بالبعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r2.claim: The person should reflect on what God made him from, reasoning that the One who began him from a drop can restore him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p408/r2.anchor: أي من أي شيء خلقه الله، والمعنى: فلينظر نظر التفكير والاستدلال حتى يعرف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r3.claim: The human is asked to consider what substance his Lord created him from.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r3.anchor: { فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق } من أي شيء خلقه ربه، ثم بين فقال:

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the verses: let the human consider his origin, created from a forcefully spurting water that comes from between backbone and breast.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.anchor: Meâl: Onun için insan düşünsün neden yaratıldı? (5). Bir atılgan sudan yaratıldı (6) ki sulb ile sîneler arasından çıkar (7).

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r2.claim: The human should look at the heaven and the piercing or lofty night star, consider the inward and outward protection and surveillance over him, avoid evil, and diligently do what leads to a happy end.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r2.anchor: fevkindeki semâya ve geceleyin zulmeti delen parlak veya yüksek yıldız gibi göze gönle çarparak nefsine vârid olan Târık’a bakıp

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r3.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r3.claim: Some take the question as a rebuke that reduces the human soul to its perceptible bodily form and stresses its lowliness.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r3.anchor: Bazıları buradan nefs-i insânînin heykel-i mahsüs denilen bedenden ibaret olduğunu

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r4.claim: Elmalılı says the bodily-only reading is incomplete: the command first presents the human as a thinking observer, matching the self-awareness described in 75:14.

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.claim: The passage warns of human weakness under surveillance while displaying God's power to create, preserve, elevate, and resurrect; reflection begins the effort to purify one's secrets and rise toward God rather than become proud.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.anchor: asıl siyak yalnız o hakāreti düşündürmek değil

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.claim: A creation account in al-Muʾminūn lists nine stages: clay extract, drop, clinging form, lump, bones, flesh, new creation, death, and resurrection.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.anchor: birincisi “sülâletin min tîn”, ikincisi “nutfe”, üçüncüsü “aleka”, dördüncüsü “mudga”, beşincisi “izâm”, altıncısı “lahm”, yedincisi “halk-ı âhar”, sekizinci “mevt”, dokuzuncusu “ba‘s”tir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.claim: These verses condense the stages to recall God's preservation and power to resurrect; they begin with the most evident and immediate starting point for reflection, the spurting fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.anchor: bütün o merâtib مِمَّ خُلِقَ خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍۢ دَافِقٍۢ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌۭ mazmunlarında hulâsa edilerek

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.claim: Though modern embryology is commonly pursued for medicine rather than theology, studying human formation can infer the Creator's power and clarify moral, religious, and human duties, so Elmalılı proceeds under the command to reflect.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.anchor: yazılan eserler hep o gayeyi isdihdaf ettiklerinden dolayı ilâhiyât bakımından istidlâl ile meşgul olmazlar ise de

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.claim: God creates functions preserving both individuals and the species; reproduction is not governed by will alone, since that would disrupt the species’ increase.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.anchor: Allah sübhânehu ve teâlâ hıfz-ı şahs vezâifini îcad buyurduğu gibi hıfz-ı

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.claim: Intercourse is called the sole reproductive act from which reproduction arises.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.anchor: mâhiyeti böyle şerh olunan mücâma‘at, tevâlüdün neş’et eylediği yegâne fi‘l-i tenâsülîdir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.claim: Intercourse is only preparatory, bringing together and depositing materials from male and female regardless of whether will governs it.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.anchor: Lâkin irâde bunu gerek istîlâ etsin gerek etmesin, her hâlde bu fiil, techîzî (ihzârî) bir fiilden başka bir şey değildir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.claim: Attention to human creation from a drop helps people recognize themselves and the deliberate Creator, an especially evident proof of divine power.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.anchor: Bu vechile insanın nutfeden hilkatine nazar-ı dikkati celbetmenin fâidesi de pek büyüktür

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.claim: The body’s extraordinary composition and the transformation of a lowly substance like mucus into a rational, remembering, aspiring human prove the Creator’s existence and power.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.anchor: insanın bedeninde terkîbât-ı acîbe ekserdir. Binâen‘aleyh onun sümük gibi hakir ve basit görünen bir maddeden halkı kādir-i muhtârın vücûduna ve kudretine edeldir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r3.claim: A person knows their own condition better than other people’s, so reflection on their own creation is a more complete proof.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r3.anchor: İnsanın kendi ahvâline ıttılâ‘ı başkalarının ahvâline ıttılâ‘dan ekserdir. Onun için bu, delâlette daha etemdir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r4.claim: People continually observe birth in their children and other animals, making this evidence for the deliberate Creator especially strong.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.claim: Human creation also proves resurrection: the Creator gathers scattered components, forms them, and breathes in a soul, so He can gather them again after death.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.anchor: mevt ile o eczânın teferrukundan sonra onları cem‘e ve evvelki gibi düzgün mahluklar yapmaya kādir olduğunu itiraf elbette vâcib olur

ELMALILI:86:8-10/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r15.claim: People should reflect on their humble origin, avoid misusing their God-given power or surrendering to base impulses, remember God’s watchfulness, and strive to meet Him with a sound heart, faith, and good works.
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r15.anchor: Onun için insan neden yaratıldığına bakmalı da sulb ile terâib arası gibi bir kafes, bir geçit olan dünyada Hâlık’ın kendisine verdiği kuvveti sû’-i isti‘mâl etmemeli

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.claim: Those denying resurrection and the afterlife are urged to learn from their own creation and judge whether resurrection after death is possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.anchor: Öldükten sonra dirilmeyi ve âhiret hayatını inkâr eden insanın, kendi yaratılışına bakarak ibret alması ve öldükten sonra yeniden dirilmeyi (ba‘s), dolayısıyla âhiret gerçeğini buna göre değerlendirmesi istenmektedir

BURHAN:v3p212/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p212/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p212/r7.claim: The alif of interrogative mā is dropped after a preposition to distinguish it from relative or declarative mā, as in fīma, ʿamma, and mimma.
BURHAN:v3p212/r7.anchor: ومنه حذف ألف ما الاستفهامية مع حرف الجر للفرق بين الاستفهامية والخبرية

QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.claim: The gushing fluid comes from the father's loins and the mother's nurturing.
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.anchor: يخرج من صلب الأب ، وتربية الأم

QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.claim: Reflection on human origin urges inference to God's complete power, knowledge, and will.
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.anchor: يحثه على النظر والاستدلال حتى يعرف كمال قدرته وعلمه وإرادته

BURHAN:v1p367/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p367/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p367/r1.claim: Dividing three levels of syntactic attachment yields six kinds of pauses: five classified by the speech itself and one by a speaker's breath.
BURHAN:v1p367/r1.anchor: فقد خرج لك بحسب هذه القسمة وهى القسمة الصناعية ستة أصناف من الوقف فى الكلام خمسة منها بحسب الكلام نفسه

BURHAN:v1p367/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p367/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p367/r2.claim: A pause can occur without stopping the breath, but a breath break always includes a pause; pauses are generally optional except where syntax requires one.
BURHAN:v1p367/r2.anchor: واعلم أن الوقف فى الكلام قد يمكن أن يكون من غير انقطاع نفس وإن كان لا شىء من انقطاع النفس إلا ومعه الوقف

BURHAN:v1p367/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p367/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p367/r3.claim: Choose the best permissible pause to match the reader's breath, replenishing air for the next utterance.
BURHAN:v1p367/r3.anchor: فعليك منه أن تختار الأفضل فالأفضل بشرط أن تطابق به انقطاع نفسك لينجذب عند السكت إلى باطنك من الهواء

BURHAN:v1p367/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p367/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p367/r4.claim: Tartil helps readers pause in the proper places, and God commanded the Prophet to recite with tartil.
BURHAN:v1p367/r4.anchor: ومما يدعو إلى الوقف فى موضع الوقف الترتيل فإنه أعون شىء عليه وقد أمر الله تعالى به رسوله

BURHAN:v1p367/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p367/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p367/r5.claim: He recommends separating identical consecutive words with a pause, illustrated by خلق at the end of 86:5 and start of 86:6, and by 9:108.
BURHAN:v1p367/r5.anchor: اجتناب تكرير اللفظة الواحدة فى القرآن تكريرا من غير فصل

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#2/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that the verse was revealed about Abu al-Ashadd, who boasted he could hold fast to a hide against anyone and alone defeat ten of Hell’s nineteen keepers, with Quraysh handling the other nine.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#2/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق ﴾ قال نزلت في أبي الأشد

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r2.claim: The human in the command to consider what he was created from is Abū Ṭālib.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r2.anchor: الثالث عشر : الإنسان أبو طالب . قوله تعالى في سورة الطارق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r13.claim: The human told to consider what he was created from is identified as Abū Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r13.anchor: والسادس عشر : أبو طالب بن عبد المطلب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah's fifth use is reflection on things to derive a judgement and thereby reach knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : النظر يقال على وجوه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r11.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r11.claim: A Qur'anic sense is reflection and consideration, including the command to consider what the human being was created from.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r11.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن النظر في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

NAHHAS:v5p197/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p197/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p197/r10.claim: The command calls for reflection with the heart; its underlying form is فلينظر, with the imperative lām making the verb jussive.
NAHHAS:v5p197/r10.anchor: من نظر القلب والأصل فلينظر حذفت الكسرة لثقلها وجزم الفعل بلام الأمر

NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.claim: مِمَّ contracts from مما; the alif is deleted because ما is interrogative, and the question is complete.
NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.anchor: الأصل مما حذفت الألف لأنها استفهام وتم الكلام

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r1.claim: Al-Ṭāriq is al-Burūj's counterpart: they share a theme, while differing in discourse style and arguments, and their introductions and endings closely resemble each other.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r1.anchor: Both have the same central theme.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r2.claim: Signs in the world, within humans, and in the Creator's attributes establish that Judgement is certain; its delay is respite that removes excuses, and the deniers' end is near.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r2.anchor: should not mislead them to deny it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r3.claim: God does not hastily seize the arrogant, but when He does, no one can escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r3.anchor: when He does, no one is able to free himself from His clasp.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.claim: Human origin is a bodily fluid, not a rare substance beyond God's reach; since He made a living person from it, He can recreate him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.anchor: he is made from a drop of fluid which emanates from his own body.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.claim: Because every soul has a guardian, people should reflect on their first creation, know the Creator can restore and requite them, and act so their recorder contains what pleases them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر أن كل نفس عليها حافظ، أتبع ذلك بوصية الإنسان بالنظر في أول نشأته الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r2.claim: مِمَّ is interrogative, من is governed by خلق, and the question clause is accusative after فلينظر and suspended by the question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r2.anchor: ومم خلق: استفهام، ومن متعلقة بخلق، والجملة في موضع نصب بفلينظر، وهي معلقة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r1.claim: The fāʾ follows from the preceding account. Alusi rejects al-Ṭībī’s claim that it is an explanatory fāʾ requiring an ellipsis: the sentence is complete without deletion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r1.anchor: متفرع على ما قبله وليست الفاء لفصيحة خلافا للطيبي إذ لا يحتاج إلى حذف في استقامة الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r2.claim: If the prior guardian is God or an appointed angel, the human should recognize the watcher, know that he will return to God, and act to please Him; the verse foregrounds the way to that knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r2.anchor: فلأنه لما أثبت سبحانه أن عليه رقيبا منه تعالى حثه على النظر المعرف لذلك مع أوصافه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r3.claim: If the guardian is the intellect, the command urges its use: reflect on creation’s beginning, recognize the Creator’s power to resurrect, and prepare for the return.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r3.anchor: وأما على تقدير أن يكون المراد به العقل فلأنه لما أثبت سبحانه أن له عقلا يرشد إلى المصالح ويكف عن المضار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r4.claim: In مم خلق, من is governed by خلق; the interrogative clause is accusative after ينظر and is suspended by its question form.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96/r4.anchor: ومم خلق استفهام ومن متعلقة بخلق والجملة في موضع نصب بينظر وهي معلقة بالأستفهام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r1.claim: A person should look thoughtfully at what kind of thing his Lord created him from.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r1.anchor: أي من أي شيء خلقه ربه، أي فلينظر نظر المتفكر.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.claim: The sūra’s purpose is to exalt the Qurʾān’s truthfulness about the reward of believers and punishment of disbelievers at Judgment, when every hidden secret is exposed and recorded.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.anchor: في يوم القيامة حين تبلى السرائر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.claim: The name al-Ṭāriq best signals this true promise when one reflects on the oath and the matter sworn to.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.anchor: واسمها الطارق أدل ما فيها على هذا الموعود الصادق بتأمل القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r1.claim: The guardian records each soul’s deeds for the King to judge, leading to the command that the human examine its origin.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r2.claim: The command is to look with insight and reflection.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r3.claim: The human is the self-absorbed person who admires himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r3.anchor: أي الآنس بنفسه الناظر في عطفه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r4.claim: The passive construction omits the maker because creation itself points to the agent, whose identity need not be named and whose craft no one else can produce.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r4.anchor: وبنى للمفعول العامل في من أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.claim: Examining one’s beginning proves the return: whoever could originate the human can certainly resurrect it; this should make a person ensure the recording angels write only what pleases God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.anchor: قدر على الابتداء قدر على الإعادة قطعا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r6.claim: The origin should command full attention because recognizing it brings eternal happiness, but human weakness and distraction make God explain the answer.

DURR-FULL:v8p474/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p474/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p474/r6.claim: Ikrima identifies the human as Abu al-Ashaddayn, who boasted he could not be removed from a hide and could handle ten of Hell’s nineteen keepers.
DURR-FULL:v8p474/r6.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة في قوله: {فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق} قال: هو أبو الأشدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r2.claim: The command to inspect the first creation follows from 86:4 and indirectly proves resurrection: a second creation is no harder than the first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r2.anchor: الفاء لتفريع الأمر بالنظر في الخلقة الأولى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r3.claim: The implied argument is: if resurrection seems impossible, inspect your origin; this fāʾ makes the omitted premise understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r3.anchor: فالتقدير : فإن رأيتم البعث محالا فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r4.claim: نظر means intellectual reflection that leads to knowledge by inference; the command addresses deniers of resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r4.anchor: وهو التفكر المؤدي إلى علم شيء بالاستدلال فالمأمور به نظر المنكر للبعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r5.claim: من is an origin preposition governed by خلق; it is fronted with interrogative ما, asking what substance the human was created from.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r6.claim: The interrogative ما makes نظر cease to take a direct object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r6.anchor: استفهامية علقت فعل النظر العقلي عن العمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r7.claim: The question awakens people to necessary knowledge, comparable to asking what the human was created from in 80:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r7.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في الإيقاظ والتنبيه إلى ما يجب علمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r8.claim: The alif of interrogative ما is omitted when it is governed by a preposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r8.anchor: وحذف ألف ( ما ) الاستفهامية على طريقة وقوعها مجرورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r9.claim: Because this is not a genuine request for information, the speaker answers it with another question, as in 78:1–2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r9.anchor: ولكون الاستفهام غير حقيقي أجاب عنه المتكلم بالاستفهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r10.claim: الإنسان here means specifically the denier of resurrection, as the command’s connection shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r10.anchor: مراد به خصوص منكر البعث كما علمت آنفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r5.claim: This challenges resurrection deniers to consider their origin; the answer follows swiftly to prove resurrection possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق، توقيف لمنكري البعث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82/r1.claim: The command is to reflect on what God created the human from: since He began creation from a sperm drop, He can restore the dead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82/r1.anchor: أي من أي شيء خلقه الله والمعنى فلينظر نظر التفكر والاستدلال ليعرف أن الذي ابتدأه من نطفة قادر على إعادته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r1.claim: The command reminds people of their weak origin and guides them to acknowledge resurrection: the One able to begin creation can all the more readily restore it, as 30:27 says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r1.anchor: تنبيه للإنسان على ضعف أصله الذي خلق منه، وإرشاد له إلى الاعتراف بالمعاد؛ لأن من قدر على البداءة فهو قادر على الإعادة

JISHUMI:v10p7367/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r3.claim: The command requires reflection on one’s body, structure, form, and changes from one state to another, to recognize a maker and governor.
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فلينظر) على وجوب النظر في نفسه وتراكيبه وصورته، وتنقله من حال إلى حال؛ ليعلم أن له صانعا ومدبرا.

JISHUMI:v10p7367/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r4.claim: The first duty is to consider the path to knowing God, since every sound act of knowledge or worship depends on knowing Him.
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r4.anchor: قلنا: النظر في طريق معرفته تعالى؛ لأنه لا شيء من العلم والعمل إلا وصحته موقوفة على معرفة الله تعالى.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r1.claim: After saying every soul has a guardian, the text urges reflection on humanity’s first creation: the Creator can restore and recompense, so one should prepare for that day and give the guardian a pleasing record.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r1.anchor: أن على كل نفس حافظا ، أتبعه توصية الإنسان بالنظر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.claim: The question from what was he created is answered by he was created from a spurting fluid.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.anchor: { مم خلق } استفهام جوابه { خلق من ماء دافق }

MUQATIL:86:1-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:86:1-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:86:1-7/r3.claim: If a person does not believe in resurrection, he should consider what he was created from.
MUQATIL:86:1-7/r3.anchor: فإن لا يصدق هذا الإنسان بالبعث { فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r1.claim: Since each soul has a watcher, reflection on human origins shows that the Creator can resurrect and requite him; one should work for Judgment Day and dictate only what will please the recorder in the end.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r1.anchor: لما ذكر أن على كل نفس حافظا أمره بالنظر فى أول أمره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r2.claim: The phrase is an interrogative asking from what thing man was created; its answer follows in the next verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331/r2.anchor: ومم خلق استفهام أى من أى شئ

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r1.claim: The passage directs people to consider their first origin so they know the one who created them can restore and recompense them; they should prepare for resurrection and give their recorders only deeds that benefit them.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r1.anchor: وجه الاتصال بما قبله توصية الإنسان بالنظر في أول أمره وسنته الأولى، حتى يعلم أن من أنشأه قادر على إعادته وجزائه

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r2.claim: Al-insan here means the son of Adam.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فلينظر الإنسان } أي ابن آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r3.claim: “Mimma khuliqa” is an interrogative: from what was he created? “Khuliqa” supplies the answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r3.anchor: و { مم خلق }؟ استفهام أي من أي شيء خلق؟ ثم قال: { خلق } وهو جواب الاستفهام

QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r1.claim: Quṭb moves from a cosmic touch connecting the soul to the universe to one affirming God's decree and governance, as sworn by heaven and the nightcomer.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r1.anchor: تؤكد حقيقة التقدير والتدبير ،  التي أقسم عليها بالسماء والطارق

QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.claim: Humanity's first creation demonstrates divine determination and governance, showing that people are not abandoned aimlessly or left neglected.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.anchor: وتوحي بأن الإنسان ليس متروكا سدى ،  ولا مهملا ضياعا

QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r3.claim: The human should consider what he was created from and what he has become.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r3.anchor: فلينظر الإنسان من أي شيء خلق وإلى أي شيء صار
